produced_by: iam:SimulateCustomPolicy via boto3, profile mainline-dev, region ap-southeast-1. Read-only; no AWS resource was created, modified or read for its contents.

source_of_truth.inline_policy: module.api[0].aws_iam_role_policy.dsn_access .change.after.policy (verbatim, account id already masked in the plan)

side_effects_disclosure.what: One AWS resource came into existence during this pass. It was not intended and it is disclosed rather than omitted.
side_effects_disclosure.effect: AWS KMS creates the AWS managed key behind a predefined AWS alias on first DescribeKey. Before the call the account held 0 KMS keys in ap-southeast-1 and alias/aws/ssm had TargetKeyId null (the deploy-verify lead measured this in plan2 section 0.4). After it, alias/aws/ssm resolves to a key created at 2026-08-12T12:46:08Z, seconds after the call.
side_effects_disclosure.impact: None material. KeyManager=AWS, so it is not billable (the USD 1/month key charge applies to customer managed keys only), it cannot be scheduled for deletion by the account, and writing the DSN SecureString would have created it anyway. No Terraform resource addresses it; the plan is unchanged. It does invalidate one row of the lead's section 0.4 table.
side_effects_disclosure.no_other_mutations: Every other call in this pass was iam:GetPolicy, iam:GetPolicyVersion, iam:SimulateCustomPolicy, kms:GetKeyPolicy, kms:ListKeys, kms:ListAliases, sts:GetCallerIdentity. No terraform was run.

kms_key_policy_alias_aws_ssm.note: Fetched live with kms:GetKeyPolicy. This is the OTHER half of the authorization for the decrypt: an identity policy and a key policy must both allow. It shows the aws/ssm key already pins kms:ViaService and kms:CallerAccount, and does NOT pin PARAMETER_ARN — so the parameter-level scoping exists only in the identity policy under test.

Statement.Sid: Allow access through SSM for all principals in the account that are authorized to use SSM
Allow direct access to key metadata to the account

simulations.why_this_matters: db.py:184 issues AmazonSSM.GetParameter for exactly this Name. This is the only SSM call the deployed code makes; if this were denied every DB-backed route would answer 503 dsn_unavailable.

db.py:184 sends WithDecryption:true, so SSM calls kms:Decrypt on the caller's behalf with ViaService=ssm.ap-southeast-1 and EncryptionContext PARAMETER_ARN set to the parameter. Both conditions satisfied.
ssm:GetParameters (batch) is a distinct action and is absent from the policy. The module claims it is absent; this proves it.
ssm:GetParametersByPath would enumerate every parameter under /mainline/demo. Absent from the policy.
ssm:DescribeParameters lists parameter metadata account-wide (it takes Resource *). Absent from the policy.
Write-back on the one ARN the role can read. A compromised handler cannot overwrite the DSN to point the demo at an attacker's database.
Sibling path under the same /mainline prefix. Proves the grant is one ARN, not parameter/mainline/*.
Unrelated tenant path in the shared account. Proves no cross-project read.
Same parameter name in ap-southeast-2 (where Bedrock lives). The ARN pins the region, so a region-confused caller gets nothing.
Ciphertext of a DIFFERENT SecureString under the same aws/ssm key: SSM supplies that parameter's ARN as encryption context, the StringEquals fails. This is the test that makes Resource:* safe.
Encryption context absent entirely (a raw kms:Decrypt of arbitrary ciphertext). StringEquals on an absent key never matches.
Right encryption context, wrong calling service. A decrypt routed through Secrets Manager or called directly by the role is refused.

FINDING. W1 predicted implicitDeny and got allowed. The condition key name, including the context-key suffix after kms:EncryptionContext:, is NOT case sensitive: 'A policy that uses this condition does not check the case of either element of the condition key' (AWS KMS Developer Guide, conditions-kms.html). So a decrypt whose encryption context key is spelled parameter_arn also satisfies the policy. Not exploitable — SSM only ever sets PARAMETER_ARN — but the condition is one character looser than it reads.
Only Decrypt is granted. Encrypt/GenerateDataKey/DescribeKey/ReEncrypt are not, even with a perfect encryption context.
AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole. Needed: the runtime writes every INIT/START/END/REPORT line and app.py's logging.getLogger output into this stream.
OVER-GRANT PROOF. The same managed policy permits creating a log group and writing log events into another team's function's log group in us-east-1. Resource is a bare *, unconditioned.
Bounding the over-grant: the managed policy is write-only. It cannot read back (FilterLogEvents/GetLogEvents) or destroy (DeleteLogGroup) any log data.
The role as it will exist (both documents together). Every other AWS service the repo touches elsewhere is unreachable from this function.

The condition VALUE is compared by the operator, and StringEquals is case-sensitive. A parameter named .../COCKROACH_DSN is a different parameter and is refused. Complements S13: key NAME casing is ignored, value casing is not.

kms:ViaService is only populated when an integrated service makes the call. A kms:Decrypt issued directly by the role (arbitrary ciphertext, correct encryption context) has no ViaService and is refused.
AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole in isolation cannot read the DSN parameter. The two documents are independent; the wildcard in the managed policy is confined to logs:* actions.
